title: Tuna Noodle Casserole with Vegetables and Mushroom Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Tuna noodle casserole with vegetables and mushroom sauce is a baked dish that combines flaked tuna with pasta, a mix of vegetables (such as carrots, peas, broccoli) and a creamy mushroom sauce made from mushrooms and cream. The dish is popular in North America as a quick, comforting family dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned tuna is often used in casseroles because it is shelf‑stable and inexpensive.
The mushroom sauce adds a rich umami flavor and a silky texture.
In the United States the casserole is traditionally made with short pasta like elbow macaroni or shells.
Adding vegetables boosts the content of vitamins A, C and dietary fiber, making the meal more balanced.
The dish is frequently served in individual ceramic dishes, which makes reheating in a microwave convenient.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Tuna provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Tuna contains EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The casserole supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Vegetables add dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Moderate saturated fat
items.content: When made with low‑fat milk or cream, the dish remains relatively low in saturated fat.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Tuna can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content in canned tuna
items.content: Canned tuna is often salted; choose low‑sodium varieties when possible.

items.title: Heavy metal exposure
items.content: Tuna may contain trace amounts of mercury; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Lactose in the sauce
items.content: If the sauce is made with dairy, people with lactose intolerance should use alternatives.

items.title: Overcooked pasta
items.content: Over‑cooking the noodles can make them mushy and affect the casserole’s texture.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the casserole hot, usually in individual ramekins. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, dill) or a sprinkle of grated cheese. Leftovers reheat well in the oven or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked casserole in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
